title: Long-term effectiveness of app-based therapy for female urinary incontinence: 48-week follow-up of a randomised controlled trial

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Long-term effectiveness of app-based therapy for female urinary incontinence: 48-week follow-up of a randomised controlled trial》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0055】Previous follow-up studies demonstrated clinically meaningful symptom improvement but differ from the present programme in scope and design. One app addressed stress incontinence only,10 and a separate app subsequently addressed urgency and mixed incontinence with a multimodal programme.11 Another multimodal programme included all subtypes, with effectiveness maintained at one year, but was evaluated in primary care under a non-inferiority design against usual care.12 Evidence therefore remains limited for a multimodal digital therapeutic that has undergone national regulatory approval, beyond medical-device certification alone, evaluated across all subtypes with respect to durability, delayed versus immediate access, and objective usage–response relationships.

【Introduction · p0060】We conducted a prespecified 48-week follow-up of the DINKS (Digital Incontinence Study) trial which included data from the early app group and from the late app group (waiting group) at baseline, week 12, 24, 36, and 48 to address these evidence gaps. We hypothesised that improvements achieved with app-based therapy would be maintained for at least 48 weeks. As a descriptive objective, we estimated the difference in outcomes between immediate and 12-week-delayed initiation at equivalent post-intervention intervals; no non-inferiority margin was prespecified.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Long-term effectiveness of app-based therapy for female urinary incontinence: 48-week follow-up of a randomised controlled trial》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study design and participants · p0075】After the initial 12-week randomized controlled trial (RCT), the control group received access to the app-based programme and both groups were surveyed at 12-week intervals until they reached week 48. Initiation of new therapies were assessed at every time point. Data acquisition and management from baseline through week 48 were performed by an independent contract research organization CW-Research & Management (Munich, Germany) using electronic case report forms (eCRF) implemented in DACIMA (EvidentIQ, Hamburg, Germany) and questionnaire-based assessments administered via LimeSurvey (LimeSurvey GmbH, Hamburg, Germany). Participants received automated email reminders with the link to the eCRF. Data quality was ensured through built-in validation checks, regular monitoring, and audit trails, and access to the final dataset was restricted to authorised study personnel. All data handling complied with General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and institutional data protection requirements.

【Study design and participants · p0065】DINKS was a single-blind, waitlist-controlled, randomised trial, reported in accordance with Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials (CONSORT) guidelines, as previously reported.9 Briefly, participants with stress, urge, or mixed urinary incontinence were recruited between April 30 and September 2, 2024, by 239 office urologists and gynaecologists from all regions of Germany. Eligible participants were adults (aged ≥ 18 years) assigned female at birth with stress, urge, or mixed urinary incontinence as defined by their treating urologist or gynaecologist, with at least one urinary incontinence episode per day. Ownership of a smartphone or tablet was required for study participation. Participants were permitted to continue pre-existing therapies that had been initiated more than 4 weeks before enrolment, including bladder-specific or incontinence medications. The initiation of new therapies during the study was documented at the outcome assessment.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Long-term effectiveness of app-based therapy for female urinary incontinence: 48-week follow-up of a randomised controlled trial》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Findings · abstract-3-1】Data availability declined progressively from 186 of 194 participants (95.9%) at week 12-66 (34.0%) at week 48. Pooled improvements exceeded the minimal clinically important difference at 12, 24, and 36 weeks after therapy start (ICIQ-UI-SF at 36 weeks -4.13, 95% Confidence Interval (CI) -4.80 to -3.47), and 73-77% of participants met the responder threshold. Differences between immediate and delayed initiation were small (ICIQ-UI-SF at 36 weeks 0.08, -1.09 to 1.25). The week-48 estimate (-3.88, -4.74 to -3.03) was intervention-group only, from 27 of 96. No adverse events were reported.

【Introduction · p0050】The initial 12-week results of the Digital Incontinence Study (DINKS) demonstrated that app-based therapy combining pelvic floor training, bladder training, cognitive behavioural strategies, and lifestyle guidance significantly reduced incontinence episode frequency (mean relative reduction 60.95%, 95% CI −71.7 to −46.7; p < 0.001) and improved symptom severity as measured by the ICIQ-UI-SF (International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire–Urinary Incontinence Short Form) (mean difference −3.94 points, 95% CI −4.74 to −3.14; p < 0.001) compared with usual care alone.9 Additionally, the intervention reduced pad usage by 2.63 pads per day (relative decrease 27.8%), with a between-group treatment effect of 2.6 pads (95% CI 1.6–3.5; p < 0.0001).9

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Long-term effectiveness of app-based therapy for female urinary incontinence: 48-week follow-up of a randomised controlled trial》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Fig. 1 · fig1】Fig. 1 CONSORT flow diagram. Flow diagram showing participant progression through the trial from enrolment through 48-week follow-up. The intervention group (IG) received immediate app-based therapy; the control group (CG) received therapy after a 12-week waitlist period. ITT = intention-to-treat. CC = complete cases. N = number of participants. Full analysis set/ ITT (primary): all randomised participants (n = 194), analysed as randomised, missing data handled by MI-MAR. Complete-case set (sensitivity): participants with observed data at the relevant timepoint. Safety set: all participants who accessed the app; no adverse events were reported in either group, so a separate safety tabulation was not warranted.

【Fig. 2 · fig2】Fig. 2 Time-aligned between-group comparisons of change from baseline over 48 weeks. CfB–Change from Baseline; CI–confidence interval; IG–intervention group; CG–control group; ICIQ-UI-SF–International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire–Urinary Incontinence Short Form; I-QoL–Incontinence Quality of Life. (A) ICIQ-UI-SF scores. (B) I-QoL scores. Data are MI-MAR imputed means with shaded areas representing 95% confidence intervals. The intervention group (blue) is plotted by calendar week; the control group (orange) is time-aligned to intervention start (i.e., control group week 24 is aligned with intervention group week 12, both representing 12 weeks post-intervention). The black horizontal line indicates null (no change); the dashed red line indicates the minimal clinically important difference (ICIQ-UI-SF: 2.0 points; I-QoL: 6.3 points). Black triangles indicate MI-MAR–adjusted mean differences between groups at corresponding post-intervention timepoints. Incontinence Short Form. I-QoL = Incontinence Quality of Life questionnaire. MI-MAR = multiple imputation under missing-at-random assumption.

【Fig. 3 · fig3】Fig. 3 Pooled cohort trajectory of change from baseline aligned to intervention start. CfB–Change from Baseline; CI–confidence interval; IG–intervention group; CG–control group; ICIQ-UI-SF–International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire–Urinary Incontinence Short Form; I-QoL–Incontinence Quality of Life; w-week. (A) ICIQ-UI-SF scores. (B) I-QoL scores. Both groups are combined and aligned to their respective intervention start dates (intervention group: week 0; control group: week 12). Data are MI-MAR imputed means (n = 194 for 12–36 weeks post-intervention; n = 96 [IG only] for 48 weeks post-intervention, 27 of 96 with observed data) with shaded areas representing 95% confidence intervals. The black horizontal line indicates null (no change); the dashed line indicates the minimal clinically important difference. All improvements exceeded the MCID at every timepoint (all p < 0.001).

sections.title: 复现线索
sections.text:
《Long-term effectiveness of app-based therapy for female urinary incontinence: 48-week follow-up of a randomised controlled trial》：复现时可直接核对的数据、软件或实现线索。

【Statistical analysis · p0150】The DINKS statistical analysis plan was prespecified for the randomised phase of the trial and covers the analyses through the primary 12-week endpoint. The follow-up assessment timepoints (weeks 24, 36, and 48) were prespecified in the study protocol; however, the statistical analyses applied to these follow-up data were not specified in the analysis plan and are therefore exploratory. Accordingly, all analyses in this extended follow-up are descriptive and hypothesis-generating, and reported p-values are local, without adjustment for multiple comparisons. Statistical significance was set at two-sided α = 0.05. Analyses were conducted using R version 4.3.1 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing).
